name: Chicken Kathi Roll
cuisine: Kolkata (Bengali street food; sold across India, including Mumbai)

ingredients.name: Oil (groundnut, sunflower or mustard oil), for the chicken

equipment: Tawa (flat griddle) or a heavy flat frying pan, at least 24 cm, for the paratha
Small kadai or frying pan for the chicken
3 small bowls (chicken marinade, dough, onion), a fork for beating the egg, a spatula (a wide, thin one makes flipping easier)
Butter paper, foil or a paper napkin, to wrap the bottom half of the roll, Kolkata-style

steps.title: Cut the chicken
steps.text: Cut 100 g boneless chicken into strips about 1.5 cm thick and 4–5 cm long.
steps.tip: Even sizes cook evenly. Thigh stays juicier than breast in a hot pan.
steps.visualCue: Even strips with no large chunks
steps.cameraCheck: The cut strips on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing chicken thigh into strips.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the chicken with 20 g curd, 5 g ginger-garlic paste, 1 g (½ tsp) Kashmiri chilli powder, a pinch of turmeric, 0.5 g (¼ tsp) garam masala, 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice and 1 g (scant ¼ tsp) salt. Cover and refrigerate.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, knife and board with soap after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: Every strip coated in a thick orange-red paste
steps.cameraCheck: The marinated chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon folding chicken strips through red marinade.

steps.title: Start the dough
steps.text: In a bowl, mix 50 g maida with a pinch (0.5 g) of salt and 5 ml (1 tsp) oil. Rub the oil in with your fingertips.
steps.visualCue: The flour looks like damp sand and holds a shape when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: The flour mixture pressed in your fist
steps.videoShot: Fingertips rubbing oil into flour.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Add about 25 ml water a teaspoon at a time, and knead into a smooth, soft dough.
steps.tip: Too sticky? Add a pinch of flour. Too stiff? Wet your hand and knead again.
steps.visualCue: Soft, smooth and not sticky; a finger dent springs back slowly
steps.videoShot: The heel of a hand pushing and folding the dough.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Smear a drop of oil on the dough ball, cover the bowl and leave it.
steps.tip: Rested dough rolls thin without shrinking back.
steps.visualCue: The dough feels more relaxed and stretchy after resting
steps.videoShot: A plate placed over the bowl of dough.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Slice 40 g onion into thin half-moons.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even slices that separate into strands
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing an onion into thin crescents.

steps.title: Season the onion
steps.text: In a small bowl, toss the onion with 2 g chopped green chilli, 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice, 0.5 g chaat masala, a tiny pinch of salt and 2 g chopped coriander.
steps.tip: The lemon takes the raw sting out of the onion (Bong Eats does the same).
steps.visualCue: The onion turns slightly glossy and softens at the edges
steps.videoShot: Fingers tossing onion with lemon and green flecks of coriander.

steps.title: Beat the egg
steps.text: Crack 1 egg into a bowl and beat it with a fork.
steps.visualCue: Evenly yellow, a little frothy, no streaks of white
steps.videoShot: A fork whisking an egg in a small bowl.

steps.title: Heat the oil for the chicken
steps.text: Heat 5 ml (1 tsp) oil in the pan on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers (mustard oil: heat until it just smokes, then lower the heat slightly)
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in a hot pan.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Lay the chicken strips in a single layer, shaking off extra marinade. Leave them untouched.
steps.tip: Don't crowd or stir them too early, or they steam instead of browning.
steps.visualCue: A loud sizzle; the undersides turn brown with dark spots
steps.videoShot: Red-coated strips hitting the sizzling pan.

steps.title: Cook the chicken through
steps.text: Turn the strips and cook, turning every minute, until cooked through and slightly charred at the edges. Add any leftover marinade in the last minute and cook it dry.
steps.tip: Breast cooks about 1 min faster than thigh. Thick pieces may need 1–2 min more on low heat with the pan covered.
steps.visualCue: Browned edges, no wet marinade left in the pan, juices run clear
steps.cameraCheck: One strip cut open (white all through, no pink)
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning charred chicken strips.

steps.title: Remove the chicken
steps.text: Move the chicken to a plate. Wipe the pan clean if you are using it for the paratha.
steps.visualCue: The pan is empty and wiped
steps.cameraCheck: The cooked chicken on the plate
steps.videoShot: Chicken strips slid onto a plate.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: A sprinkle of water sizzles and disappears in 2–3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: The water drops sizzling on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Water droplets dancing on the hot tawa.

steps.title: Roll out the paratha
steps.text: Knead the dough 10 seconds, flatten it, dust with a little flour and roll it into a thin round, 20–22 cm across.
steps.tip: For flaky layers (lachha style), roll it to 12 cm, smear ¼ tsp of the cooking oil, roll it up like a rope, coil it into a spiral, rest 2 min and roll it out again.
steps.visualCue: Thin enough to almost see the board through it, with an even thickness
steps.cameraCheck: The rolled paratha next to a 20 cm plate
steps.videoShot: The rolling pin pushing the dough into a wide circle.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Lay the paratha on the tawa and cook.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles appear and the underside has light brown spots
steps.videoShot: Bubbles rising on the raw paratha.

steps.title: Cook the second side with oil
steps.text: Flip it, drizzle 2.5 ml (½ tsp) oil over it and spread. Cook, then flip again and add the other 2.5 ml (½ tsp) oil.
steps.visualCue: Both sides golden with brown spots; it puffs in places
steps.videoShot: A spoon spreading oil over the paratha.

steps.title: Add the egg
steps.text: Pour the beaten egg over the top of the paratha and spread it right to the edges with the back of a spoon.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even yellow layer covering the paratha
steps.cameraCheck: The egg spread on the paratha
steps.videoShot: Beaten egg poured and spread in a circle.

steps.title: Cook the egg side
steps.text: Flip the paratha quickly so the egg side is on the tawa, and press gently with the spatula.
steps.tip: Flip in one quick, confident move with a wide spatula. A little runny egg on the tawa is fine; push it back under.
steps.visualCue: The egg is set, pale golden and stuck to the paratha, with no wet patches
steps.cameraCheck: The egg side, after lifting one edge
steps.videoShot: The spatula flipping the paratha onto the sizzling egg.

steps.title: Take it off
steps.text: Flip once more and slide the paratha onto a plate, egg side up.
steps.visualCue: A golden paratha with an egg layer on top
steps.cameraCheck: The paratha on the plate, egg side up
steps.videoShot: The paratha sliding off the tawa onto a plate.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Lay the chicken in a line across the paratha, about a third of the way in from one edge.
steps.visualCue: A neat line of chicken from one side to the other, with 2 cm left clear at each end
steps.videoShot: Chicken strips laid in a row.

steps.title: Add the onion and sauce
steps.text: Spoon the onion mix over the chicken and drizzle 10 g (2 tsp) ketchup on top.
steps.visualCue: Pink-white onion and red sauce over the chicken
steps.videoShot: A zigzag of ketchup over the onions.

steps.title: Roll it
steps.text: Fold the near edge over the filling and roll it up tightly.
steps.visualCue: A firm, even cylinder with the filling showing at the ends
steps.cameraCheck: The rolled roll, seam side down
steps.videoShot: Hands rolling the paratha into a tight cylinder.

steps.title: Wrap and serve
steps.text: Wrap the bottom half in butter paper or foil and serve hot.
steps.visualCue: Half wrapped, half open, Kolkata-style
steps.videoShot: The roll twisted into paper and cut in half to show the layers.

reasons: a strong 33 g of protein from pan-seared (not deep-fried) chicken and egg, with only 3 tsp of oil in all and fresh onion, lemon and coriander. Points come off for the refined-flour paratha (low fibre, about 3 g), cholesterol (about 280 mg, mostly the egg yolk), sodium (about 1,000 mg) and few vegetables. Restaurant rolls usually use more oil or dalda on the paratha, mayonnaise or extra sauces, sometimes two eggs, and more salt; many delivery rolls are 550–650 kcal.

researchRating.basis: the Kolkata kathi roll is one of India's best-known street foods, credited to Nizam's in Kolkata and copied across the country (Wikipedia, Gulf News). Recipe pages are rated highly: Ministry of Curry about 4.85/5 (26 votes), Cook with Kushi about 4.89/5 (9 votes), Madhura's Recipe 5/5 (1 vote). Mumbai guides name roll shops such as Ayub's (Kala Ghoda) and Hangla's as favourites (LBB, The Quint, Homegrown, Free Press Journal). Small deduction: the vote counts are small, and reviews often complain of dry or undercooked chicken, high prices for small rolls (Ayub's reviewers) and weak chicken rolls at chains (one food blogger on Hangla's).

storage: An assembled roll goes soggy, so store the parts separately. Cooked chicken: fridge in a closed box for up to 2 days; freezer up to 1 month. Raw dough: fridge up to 1 day, wrapped. Marinated raw chicken: fridge up to 24 hours. Cooked egg parathas: fridge up to 1 day. Don't leave the cooked chicken out for more than 2 hours. Reheat the chicken in a pan with a splash of water until steaming hot (2–3 min), and warm the paratha on a hot tawa for 20–30 seconds per side, then roll it fresh. An already-rolled leftover can be reheated on a tawa, turning, for 3–4 min, or in a microwave for 40–60 seconds (it will be softer).
leftoverRemix: kathi roll chicken fried rice (or "roll bowl"). Shred leftover chicken and paratha into small pieces, and toss them in a hot pan with 1 tsp oil, the leftover onion mix, a handful of cooked rice or chopped cabbage, a splash of soy or chilli sauce and a fried egg on top. Or tear the paratha into strips for a quick Kothu-style stir-fry. Use within the same 2-day window and reheat only once.
burnOff: about 7.8 km of running (545 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.9 km of brisk walking (about 2 hours 10 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: contains chicken, egg, maida, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided in the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains chicken, egg, grain (maida) and onion-garlic, avoided under the common Ekadashi rule set.

jain.reason: contains chicken and egg, plus onion, garlic and ginger (root).

ramadan.reason: use halal chicken. A filling, high-protein roll for iftar, but at about 1,000 mg sodium (est.) it is salty for sehri unless you cut the salt and skip the ketchup and chaat masala.

jain.reason: contains chicken and egg, plus onion and garlic.

sattvik.reason: contains chicken, egg, onion and garlic.

glutenFree.reason: the paratha is maida (refined wheat flour). Chaat masala blends can also contain hing, which is usually compounded with wheat flour in India. A gluten-free version is in the Diet variants (section 4).

dairyFree.reason: leave out the 20 g curd in the marinade and use 5 ml more lemon juice. No ghee or butter is used.

description: A non-veg Kolkata egg-and-chicken roll: tikka-style chicken and lemony onions in an egg-coated maida paratha; gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian and low-oil versions below.

variants.reason: the Jain diet excludes chicken and egg, and the filling relies on onion, garlic and ginger. For a meat-free roll, see the Vegetarian (paneer) variant below. A Jain version of that would also need the onion, garlic and ginger removed; this run did not check a published Jain kathi roll recipe.
the dish is defined by chicken and egg. A soya-chunk or tofu roll would be a different dish; this run did not research one.
